clue.text: Sent down in due course?

definitions.meaning: sent to prison, handed a sentence to serve
eventually, once enough time has been allowed

explanation.walkthrough: Being given time is British slang for receiving a prison sentence; 'given time' also means 'if allowed time', as in 'given time, it will heal'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are idioms: a convict is handed a term of years, and a patient result comes after waiting.

clue.text: Line on map is round and local

parts.note: a round shape resembles the letter O
a local is a British pub, and a bar is a pub too

explanation.surface: A mapmaker describes a boundary line as circular and nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' looks like an adjective; in British usage 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub, hence BAR.
explanation.definitionFit: On a weather chart, a line joining points of equal atmospheric pressure is drawn as such a line.

clue.text: In time, deserter makes mistakes

indicators.note: the deserter is placed in the word for time, inside its letters

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is someone who deserts a cause, as rats leave a sinking ship

explanation.surface: Over time, a soldier who runs away commits errors.
explanation.definitionFit: A list of corrections for printing errors is a plural word for mistakes, from Latin.

clue.text: Commonplace tourism misguided, nothing less

indicators.note: letters of the word tourism are led astray into a new order

parts.note: nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles that tourism has lost its way and amounts to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'less' tells you to take the O (nothing) away from the rearranged letters of TOURISM.
explanation.definitionFit: A platitude or self-evident statement is a commonplace, a noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Minute hot lemons in fudge taste very good

indicators.note: to fudge is to fiddle or fake, so the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: A recipe note: quickly heat the lemons into a fudge mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fudge' tempts as a sweet in the kitchen scene, but 'in fudge' is the anagram signal for MINUTE HOT LEMONS.
explanation.definitionFit: Food said to do this is delicious, an idiom for something tasting excellent.

clue.text: Have to do with apparent confusion about one

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round, about, the single letter for one
the word apparent is thrown into confusion, its letters jumbled

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is involved in obvious muddle over a single thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confusion' rearranges APPARENT to APPERTAN, and 'about' puts it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: To appertain to something is to relate or belong to it, a formal synonym.

clue.text: Getting back into society?

parts.note: reads like a released prisoner re-entering the world, but a society here is a club one renews membership of

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: a society is also a club.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming a member once more of a club or association is what this word describes, a literal sense.

clue.text: Heels, pair becoming more elegant

indicators.note: the letters of heels and pair turn into, become, a new word

explanation.surface: A pair of high heels is said to make the wearer look smarter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'becoming' could mean flattering, which suits the fashion picture, but here it says the letters change into something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a more attractive, well-proportioned figure is to be more elegant in form.

clue.text: Address where one left ripening peaches

indicators.note: fruit changes as it ripens, so the letters of peaches change order

parts.note: one is the indefinite article, a single item, giving A

explanation.surface: Someone talks about the place where a person left peaches to ripen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' says the A (one) goes from the reworked letters of PEACHES.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal talk given to an audience is an address, a noun synonym.

clue.text: Isn't money in Moscow easy!

parts.note: is not, giving the negative word not
the rouble is the currency of Russia, whose capital is Moscow

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that a Russian banknote is simple to obtain.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is no bother or easy is an idiom for a task that gives no difficulty.

clue.text: Get back about 100 publishers

parts.note: re is Latin for concerning, about
C is the Roman numeral for 100
OUP is Oxford University Press, a publisher

explanation.surface: A publisher recovers money from a hundred rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover money one has lost or spent is to get it back.

clue.text: Brilliant but wayward anti-Fascist is leaving

indicators.note: unruly, straying from the expected path, so the letters wander

explanation.surface: A rebellious opponent of fascism is departing, which is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' says IS is taken out of the reworked letters of ANTI-FASCIST.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fantastic is excellent, superb; an informal synonym for brilliant.

clue.text: Without a key that's found in coat on a line

indicators.note: the answer sits found in the run of letters coat on a line

explanation.surface: A garment hung on a washing line has no key in its pocket.
explanation.definitionFit: Music written with no key or tonal centre is described with this term.

clue.text: Duck on paper cover

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck
something written down is on paper

explanation.surface: A duck is pictured on the cover of a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A quilt stuffed with soft feathers is a bed cover, originally filled with duck down.

clue.text: Removed case under dish in some shallow water

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece under another comes after it

parts.note: a balti is a curry dish cooked in a metal pan

indicators.note: the letters of case are moved again, reset

explanation.surface: A packing case was taken away from beneath a dish.
explanation.walkthrough: BALTI is a curry cooked and served in a wok-like bowl, popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: This northern European sea is notably shallow, so it is an example of some shallow water.

clue.text: Redness evident in Florida city lacking air-conditioning

indicators.note: going without something means those letters are removed

explanation.surface: A sunburnt look appears in a hot Florida town without cooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being florid means ruddy in complexion, so this noun means redness of face.

clue.text: Second person who never can tell

definitions.meaning: the pronoun of the person addressed, grammatical second person
the Shaw comedy title is that word followed by 'Never Can Tell'

explanation.walkthrough: You Never Can Tell is a comedy by George Bernard Shaw; the answer supplies the 'who'.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar the second person pronoun addresses the listener, and it opens Shaw's play title.

clue.text: Lout bringing lad up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A thug is bringing up a young boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Yob is British slang for a rowdy young hooligan, a lout.

clue.text: Exploit said sheep

indicators.note: said signals a word spoken aloud matching another in sound

parts.note: ewes are female sheep

explanation.surface: Someone takes advantage of the sheep, it is reported.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit something is to make use of it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Certainly at home everyone has to study a school subject

parts.note: at home means in, as in staying in
all means everyone
to con is an old word for study or learn by heart
science is a subject taught at school

explanation.surface: Everyone at home has to study a school subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an adverb phrase, this means honestly or surely, a synonym of certainly.

clue.text: Worker has no end of meat

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for meat is dropped

parts.note: beef is a meat

explanation.surface: A labourer goes without the last of the meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker bee is the sterile female of a hive, so this insect is a classic crossword worker.

clue.text: Former wife's wrong to gain illegally

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A divorcee is wrongly trying to get money unlawfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To obtain money by force or threats is criminal, so it means to gain illegally.

clue.text: End of snow cover for three months

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of snow

parts.note: to inter is to bury, covering with earth

explanation.surface: The snow stops covering the ground after a quarter year.
explanation.definitionFit: This season lasts roughly a quarter of the year, about three months.

clue.text: Most of garment used to deaden sound

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter

parts.note: a muffler is a scarf, a garment

explanation.surface: Part of a piece of clothing is used to quieten noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To wrap or cover something so as to quieten it is to deaden its sound.

clue.text: State's wholly on edge after large number left

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above

parts.note: all means wholly

indicators.note: the large number has left, so it is removed

parts.note: taken in its everyday sense of a border
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number

explanation.surface: A country is entirely nervous once many people have departed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts ALL above EDGE, and 'left' removes D (500), giving ALLEGE from ALLEDGE.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to assert or declare, as one would state a claim.

clue.text: Little devil's one lousy criminal, in an irreverent way

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: something criminal is bent, so the letters of lousy are twisted

explanation.surface: A mischievous child is called a rotten crook, in a disrespectful manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without reverence for God or holy things is acting in an irreverent way.

clue.text: River police invited in to settle the issue

indicators.note: the police are let inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: River police are called in to resolve the matter.
explanation.definitionFit: To make up one's mind is to resolve a question, to settle the issue.

clue.text: Explained how margins were aligned

definitions.meaning: text set flush to both margins in typesetting

explanation.definitionFit: To account for an action is to give reasons; in printing, text is set level at both edges.

clue.text: Cape maybe concealing Oriental floral display

indicators.note: the cape surrounds and hides the eastern letter

parts.note: Cape Wrath is the north-west tip of Scotland
Oriental means eastern, abbreviated E

explanation.surface: A cloak might be hiding something from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cape' looks like a garment, but it is a headland: Cape Wrath in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: A ring of flowers, as laid at a funeral, is a floral display.

clue.text: Hired the red car out

indicators.note: out signals letters taken out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rented the red car to take out.
explanation.definitionFit: To charter a boat or plane is to hire it, so the past form means hired.
